chunks: And from him (Al-Saduq) from Fadalah from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not take out any part of the meat of the sacrificial animal (Hady).'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on removing parts of the meat of the sacrificial animal (Hady)?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) instructs Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar to avoid removing any part of the sacrificial animal's meat, a ruling often interpreted by Shia jurists as prohibiting the disposal of specific cuts (such as the head or limbs) or ensuring the entire animal is utilized for consumption or distribution. This emphasizes the principle of avoiding waste (israf) and maximizing the benefit of the sacrifice, aligning with the Shia emphasis on the practical utility of ritual acts. The prohibition highlights the sanctity of the Hady, ensuring that no part is treated as insignificant or discarded improperly.
